package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2 with no hotfix, 2020.2 HF 1, 2020.2 HF 2 (as per public advisories)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised to include a malicious backdoor (SUNBURST) that enabled attackers to execute arbitrary code, exfiltrate data, and maintain persistent access to victim environments. The malicious code was surreptitiously inserted into legitimate software updates, impacting thousands of organizations.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for security tools and analysis environments, waits a random interval to evade detection, then contacts a hardcoded command-and-control (C2) domain to receive further instructions or payloads, enabling remote code execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces a covert communication channel to an external C2 server, implements anti-analysis checks, and enables remote code execution, all of which are hallmarks of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain logic for external C2 communication, anti-analysis, or arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may check for updates or telemetry, but not with obfuscated C2 logic or anti-analysis features.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the SolarWinds Orion update DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll).
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of backdoor logic on customer systems.

attack_chain.action: Upon service start, the backdoor code checks for analysis environments and delays execution.
The backdoor contacts a hardcoded C2 domain to receive further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker control and possible payload delivery.

attack_chain.action: If instructed, the backdoor executes attacker-supplied code or exfiltrates data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of victim environment and data breach.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion services to rare or newly registered domains
Presence of obfuscated or suspicious logic in Orion DLLs
Anti-analysis or sandbox evasion checks in application DLLs
file_indicators: Unexpected changes in Orion DLL file hashes
network_indicators: Secondary C2 domains as per SolarWinds/SUNBURST IOCs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion service processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially to known SUNBURST C2 domains. Check Orion DLLs for hash mismatches or the presence of obfuscated code. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to identify anti-analysis logic and randomized execution patterns. Cross-reference with published IOCs from SolarWinds advisories.
